newsitem.title: USA: Latin debt firms in NY, Mexico buoyed by oil rights.
newsitem.headline: Latin debt firms in NY, Mexico buoyed by oil rights.

text.p: Despite a lackluster Treasuries market, Brady bonds added gains in New York amid a steady flow of funds, traders said.
"Every time there was profit-taking, some new buyers came in," said a Brady trader.
Argentina FRBs rose 3/8 to 80-7/8. Brazil C added 1/4 to 66-1/2.
Mexico shone among all Latin Bradies as the oil recovery rights attracted serious attention.
"Now the (oil) forwards begin to rise," said Vincent Palermo, senior quantitative strategist at Merrill Lynch. "They start to matter."

Since the U.S. missile attack on Iraq, the spot oil prices have climbed above $24 a barrel. But the Brady market has been slow to adjust to the value of oil rights imbedded in Mexican pars and discounts.
"It's hard to detach and sell," said one trader.
Lately, however, the psychology has changed as more investors believe the value of oil should be factored into Brady bond prices, he said.
Mexico pars and discounts each rose 7/8 to 67-5/8 and 83-3/4.
Nigeria, another oil exporter, also got a boost, with its Pars adding 1.00 to bid 57.00.
Venezuelan paper edged up a little, in line with Argentina and Brazil. Venezuelan pars firmed 1/4 to 65-1/4.
